To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
WalK is an ATP-binding protein and that the bound ATP molecule remains intact in the WalK crystal lattice.

the WalK histidine kinase ATP-binding domain forms a stable complex in which ATP remains intact in vivo and the ATP molecule wraps around an Mg2+ ion in an octahedral geometry, making strong interactions with the WalK protein.
the ATP binding pocket is highly specific for the ATP substrate and that this specificity may be a part of the sensing and activation mechanism of the WalK kinase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and mechanism of the WalRK two component system.
the molecular basis of bacterial cell division and cell-wall homeostasis.
the structural characterization of the WalK ATP-binding domain and its interaction with ATP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WalK-ATPK is the first two-component system ATP-binding domain structure with ATP bound in the crystal lattice.
the WalK-AMP complex is the active form of the histidine kinase.
the structure of ATP-bound WalK is a good model of the ATP-binding state of WalK in the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the ATP-bound WalK domain reveals how ATP is stabilized in the binding pocket and how ATP binding may contribute to the WalK activation mechanism.
the crystal structure of WalK-ATPPi complex is the first high-resolution structure for an intact ATP-binding domain of an essential histidine kinase.

the WalK-AD-ATP structure presented here provides a basis for further studies on the mechanism of activation of WalR by WalK and on the role of WalK in the regulation of murein synthesis and cell-division.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WalK-ADP complex is not the active state, but the WalK-AMP complex is.
the WalK-ADP complex, not WalK-ATPD, is a good starting point for the design of specific inhibitors of the WalRK system.
the WalRK two component system is poised to be activated rapidly upon the sensing of a signal.
